thirtySeconds: KeithK75 absolutely mugged the net field at Shinnecock, winning at +1 and finishing eight shots clear of HamSammich at +9. The challengers were mostly fighting for oxygen: MashedBROtato landed at +15, while Dan94 and DREADFUL both reached +27. Keith also took gross at -3, with a ridiculous 17.79 total strokes gained—8.05 on approach, 6.68 short game, and 15.35 tee to green. The net race was never really a race; it was Keith’s tournament and everybody else’s damage report.
latestTournamentTeaser: KeithK75 ran away with the net title at Shinnecock, posting +1 to beat HamSammich by eight shots. He also won gross at -3, fueled by 17.79 total strokes gained and a filthy 15.35 tee-to-green performance.

carnage.name: Dan94
carnage.commentary: The opening drive found deeprough with 269 yards still to go, and the recovery parade never really recovered: fairway, fairway, then seven yards short of the green. Two putts later, Dan finally tapped in for a nine. That is not a hole; that is a municipal-planning project.

carnage.name: IUDoc92
carnage.commentary: Deeprough off the tee, then sand, then repeated 42-yard negotiations with the fairway. From there it was 30 yards to the green and a 25-footer before the tap-in. Eight shots, one hole, and absolutely no interest in taking the direct route.

carnage.name: DREADFUL
carnage.commentary: A 119-yard par-three became deeprough, fairway, fairway, deeprough, then 19 yards short of the green. The 11-footer was left a foot away, which was the closest thing to a clean decision in the whole sequence. Seven shots and a full tour of the property.

carnage.name: Leroy4522
carnage.commentary: The drive went to deeprough, the next ball found fairway, and the approach process eventually produced a 32-footer. Then came putts from 41, 20, and 14 feet before the gimmie. Eight shots, four putts, and a hole that turned the green into an endurance event.

carnage.name: HamSammich
carnage.commentary: The first three shots all went to deeprough, moving the ball from 234 yards out to 46 yards out by sheer persistence. He finally found fairway, then green, then the six-footer for the tap-in. A seven that looked like it had to be assembled one bad decision at a time.

carnage.name: KeithK75
carnage.commentary: Keith’s worst hole still had a 264-yard drive to fairway and a 143-yard shot to green before the wheels came off. The recorded log then jumps from shot 3 to shot 5, with the next ball in deeprough and 19 yards out, followed by a 23-yard pitch and a made 11-footer. Even his disaster came with enough approach and short-game quality to escape with a seven.

carnage.name: MashedBROtato
carnage.commentary: A 130-yard par-three finished in rough, then 38 yards to fairway, then 21 yards to green. The 19-footer was pushed two feet away, and the gimmie cleaned up a five. Not catastrophic by league standards, but still a par three requiring three separate introductions to the golf course.

players.name: KeithK75
players.tagline: The fairways were optional; the score was not.
players.body: KeithK75 won both competitions, taking net at +1 and gross at -3, with HamSammich eight shots back in the net race. The raw golf was absurdly complete: 17.79 total strokes gained, including 8.05 approach, 6.68 short game, and 15.35 tee to green. He hit 10 greens, made four birdies, avoided every bogey and double bogey, and needed only 24 putts. Even the worst hole—a seven built around a deeprough detour and a recorded shot-number jump from 3 to 5—ended with a made 11-footer. Across seven prior appearances, his average net finish was 3.86 and average gross finish 1.57, with four gross wins; this was a particularly loud confirmation of that profile.

players.name: HamSammich
players.tagline: A long drive trapped inside a short-game emergency.
players.body: HamSammich took second net at +9 but finished third gross at +37, a gap explained by four greens in regulation, seven bogeys, and four doubles. He was slightly positive overall at 0.79 strokes gained, with 2.37 putting and 0.66 off the tee covering for negative approach at -2.06 and negative tee to green at -1.58. His worst hole was a seven: three straight shots into deeprough before finally reaching fairway, then a six-footer for the tap-in. The two birdies helped, but five prior appearances show the same basic tension—an average net finish of 4.6 against an average gross finish of 5.6, with total SG averaging -2.19. The net result held together; the raw ball-striking did not.

players.name: MashedBROtato
players.body: MashedBROtato finished third net at +15 and fourth gross at +39, producing 4.79 total strokes gained despite only six greens and three fairways. Approach led the charge at 3.07, with 4.77 tee to green, while putting contributed basically nothing at 0.02. Eight bogeys and two doubles kept the scorecard from cashing in on the 317-yard longest drive and 305-yard average drive distance on fairways. The worst hole was a five on a par three after rough, fairway, and green-side wandering, though he did make a 25-footer for a net double-bogey on another hole and converted both par-five birdie opportunities. With seven prior starts and an average net finish of 5.14, this was a solid raw-golf improvement over a mixed recent run, but the scoring damage still ran the show.

players.name: Dan94
players.tagline: A precision driver with one catastrophic side quest.
players.body: Dan94 was the gross runner-up at +19 but only fourth net at +27, the clearest example of the net leaderboard refusing to care about raw-golf aesthetics. He gained 6.79 overall, including 5.71 tee to green, hit eight fairways, and posted the field’s second-best gross score. Then the scorecard found eight bogeys, and the worst hole was a nine after a 229-yard drive into deeprough, two fairway recoveries, a zero-yard lie still 20 yards from the hole, and a seven-yard pitch before the putts finally stopped. His three recorded birdie-free rounds still included useful par-five work, including two gross birdies on the 16th. Seven prior appearances show a strong gross profile—average gross finish 1.71 and 11.97 total SG per appearance—but the net side remains winless, and this event did nothing to erase that split.

players.name: DREADFUL
players.tagline: The putter filed a formal complaint against gravity.
players.body: DREADFUL finished fifth net at +27 and sixth gross at +75, losing 12.21 strokes gained across every category: -6.09 tee, -1.34 approach, -0.44 short game, and -4.34 putting. Three greens, 35 putts, three three-putts, four bogeys, and eight doubles made the scorecard less a round than a long-form warning. The worst hole was a seven on a par three after the opening shot found deeprough and the next four shots bounced between fairway, deeprough, and green-side territory before a one-foot leave. He did salvage net birdies on the fifth and 16th in the third round, but seven prior starts already carried negative averages in every SG bucket and -6.33 total SG per appearance. Shinnecock confirmed the problem rather than creating a new one.

players.name: IUDoc92
players.tagline: A holed-out hero surrounded by 72 strokes of evidence.
players.body: IUDoc92 finished sixth net at +32 and fifth gross at +72, with -10.21 total strokes gained and only two greens in regulation. The damage was broad: -3.49 off the tee, -3.90 short game, and -2.36 putting, while six bogeys and six doubles overwhelmed a lone birdie. His worst hole took eight shots after deeprough off the tee, sand on the second, three more recovery attempts, and a 25-footer that finished one foot away. There was one genuine highlight—a holed-out 18-yard shot for a net eagle on the 16th—and a made nine-footer for birdie on the eighth, but they were isolated rescue flares. Across seven prior starts, his total SG average was -9.32 with a 4.29? No: his average net finish was 5.43 and average gross finish 7.0, a profile that remains heavily dependent on occasional net scoring against consistently poor raw golf.

players.name: Leroy4522
players.tagline: One green, 36 putts, and nowhere to hide.
players.body: Leroy4522 finished seventh net at +28 and seventh gross at +55, losing 11.21 total strokes gained with -3.55 off the tee, -2.04 on approach, -4.05 short game, and -1.56 putting. He hit four fairways but just one green, made no birdies, and needed 36 putts with four three-putts. His worst hole was an eight after a deeprough drive, two fairway recoveries, a 32-footer, and three more putts before the gimmie. There were a couple of clean bright spots—a net birdie on the 12th and a par on the 13th—but they could not offset the recovery workload. Seven prior appearances show a similarly difficult raw profile, with -5.74 total SG per appearance and average finishes of 6.86 net and 6.43 gross; this round reinforced the pattern rather than changing it.

stateOfLeague: KeithK75’s win strengthens an already convincing profile: seven prior starts, four gross wins, two net wins, and now another sweep with a net margin of eight shots. Dan94’s gross runner-up finish versus fourth net keeps the league’s central split alive—good raw golf does not automatically become net control—while HamSammich’s second net place came from putting and damage limitation more than ball-striking. The event confirms Keith as the current benchmark and leaves the challengers fighting to turn occasional net contention into actual wins.
